title: Mailbox shape filled with repeated placeholder letters
rationale: A conventional fill-in form for an address. The shape is grammatical but every label is a run of one letter and the top-level name is the reserved invalid name, so it is an obvious placeholder that cannot reach anyone.

reasons: Grammatically a mailbox; the placeholder reading rests on convention while the reserved top-level name only establishes that it cannot be delivered. Whether a placeholder-shaped but syntactically valid string is an identity at all is a policy question.
ambiguity.wouldSettle: A project decision, with cited reasoning, on whether placeholder-shaped valid syntax is an identity; no source was found.

provenance.inference: The invalid top-level name is reserved (cited), so the string is non-attributable; the expectation stays weaker than invalid because the grammar accepts it. Authored by an AI agent run from the cited claims and case reasoning; no scanner output was consulted; unreviewed.

title: Mailbox with a masked local part
rationale: Asterisks replace most of the local part while the domain stays intact. Not a mailbox as written, yet it narrows to one; whether a partial redaction is still personal data is not settled by the grammar.

The retained first character and full domain still partly identify the address.
ambiguity.wouldSettle: A project decision on whether partial masking is sensitive; grammar and RFC 2606 cannot settle it.

title: Role mailbox at a reserved example domain
rationale: A no-reply sender address is a function, not a person, and its domain is reserved. The grammar is valid, so identity is valid, but whether a role address is personal data is a policy question.

reasons: Syntactically a mailbox at a reserved domain.
A role address does not name an individual, but role-versus-person is not decided by the grammar; no source on role mailboxes was read.
ambiguity.wouldSettle: Read RFC 2142 and a data-protection authority text on role addresses, then decide.

provenance.inference: Role-address status is project inference; no source was read for it. Authored by an AI agent run from the cited claims and case reasoning; no scanner output was consulted; unreviewed.

title: Mailbox at the loopback host name
rationale: A one-label domain that RFC 6761 reserves for the loopback host. It parses as a mailbox but cannot name a remote person.

input.text: Run as root@localhost for the test

reasons: A single-label domain is grammatical under the RFC 5322 dot-atom rule but not a public mail domain.
The reserved name is non-attributable, which the label does not make non-sensitive in every policy.
ambiguity.wouldSettle: A project decision on whether non-attributable single-label hosts count as identities.

provenance.inference: Reserved status is from the cited section; the sensitivity reading is project inference. Authored by an AI agent run from the cited claims and case reasoning; no scanner output was consulted; unreviewed.
